## What you should be able to do tonight

- State the terminal distribution implied by geometric Brownian motion and the three stylized facts it fails.
- Say which failure the market prices and which it does not.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>60 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [30 min]{.task-min} Compare the model against your own measurements: simulate geometric Brownian motion calibrated to SPY's volatility, and run your week 6 stylized-facts test suite from day 60 on the output. It will fail on tails, on volatility clustering and on the leverage effect, and pass on the autocorrelation of returns.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [20 min]{.task-min} Say which failure has a price attached: the market quotes options at implied volatilities that vary with strike, which is the failure of the terminal distribution appearing as a price. Volatility clustering and the leverage effect appear in the term structure and the skew respectively, which is the roadmap for week 38.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [10 min]{.task-min} Write the model's assumptions as a list you will return to: constant volatility, continuous paths, frictionless trading, constant rates, no dividends unless modelled. Each of the next four weeks relaxes one.
:::
:::
